llm_proposer.assessment: The cause of svc207 is almost certainly an OTN switch-fabric failure at S08 at about t=684.3 s. The simultaneous loss of nearly every transit service through S08, while services terminating at S08 and optical power/OSNR/BER monitors remain normal, localizes the failure above the optical layer; the t=602.5 S06/och24 card failure is a separate earlier incident and does not lie on svc207.

proposals.rationale: svc207 and the large correlated outage set traverse the S08 OTN switch, while services terminating at S08 remain healthy. Unchanged optical telemetry on the surrounding line interfaces, spans, amplifiers and OCMs strongly supports an ODU-layer switch-fabric failure; the only reservation is the reported customer time preceding the bulk alarms by roughly 24 seconds.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A failed S08 WSS input could interrupt traffic without a span failure. However, affected services arrive at S08 from several degrees and leave on several degrees, and downstream optical monitoring saw no corresponding signal loss, so one WSS port cannot explain the outage pattern well.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: A bad cross-connect on svc207's ODU path could interrupt that service with normal optical measurements. It is very unlikely because it would affect one ODU rather than the simultaneous network-wide set of services transiting S08.

Failure of either svc207 client port could independently produce its service loss without optical changes. It does not explain the many simultaneous failures on unrelated services, making it only a remote coincidence.
